independent_authority_evidence.evidence_kind: Executable deterministic comparisons to independent public authority-package calls. Fixed-seed bootstrap draws verify wrapper numerical behavior, not bootstrap statistical stability; standard and moderator permutation results are also compared with direct public metafor::permutest calls. This is not a frozen RCMetaR output fixture and does not establish RC MetaStudio 0.3.1 release parity.
independent_authority_evidence.declared_method_workflow_cells: All 50 method/workflow cells have an independent authority comparison in this matrix and the direct R public-mada test. This is a method/workflow cell count, not exhaustive metric-by-input-representation coverage.
independent_authority_evidence.authority: metafor public escalc(), rma.uni(), rma.mh(), rma.peto(), and permutest() calls; boot::boot() plus direct metafor fits over the same seeded resamples; meta 8.5-0 public metabin(), metacont(), metagen(), metabias(), and trimfill() calls for small-study effects; direct metafor::regtest() for mixed-effects Egger; standard and meta-regression Reitsma direct mada calls in tests/r_stack/test_reitsma_golden.py::test_reitsma_release_values_match_public_mada_with_portable_tolerances.
independent_authority_evidence.workflow_partial_result_state_evidence: The R matrix verifies successful subset counts, study identities, and order. Incomplete and not-estimable workflow states are separately covered by tests/python/fast/test_cumulative_analysis.py, test_leave_one_out.py, test_subgroup_analysis.py, and test_subgroup_analysis_worker.py; those fast tests are semantic checks, not independent model comparisons.
independent_authority_evidence.numerical_tolerance: The method matrix and small-study model-result comparisons use 1e-8 against direct public authority values. Small-study display comparisons allow half a unit in the last place at four significant digits; bootstrap display checks allow 0.0006, and bootstrap intervals and means are checked against public boot::boot.ci() and replicate values. Reitsma uses explicit tolerances in the direct mada test. No expected outputs are captured from RCMetaR.

binary.one-arm-proportion: Raw event/total counts are checked for PR, PLN, PLO, PAS, and PFT against metafor::escalc() and fixed/random public model fits; entered PR effects are checked through the random-effects route.
binary.two-arm-proportions: Raw two-arm counts are checked for OR, RD, RR, AS, YUQ, and YUY with inverse-variance/random-effects fits; Mantel-Haenszel is checked for OR, RR, and RD. Entered comparative effects are checked for OR through the random-effects route.

continuous.one-arm-mean: Raw mean/SD/sample-size inputs are checked through metafor::escalc('MN') for the standard random model, all cumulative/leave-one-out/subgroup model methods, and bootstrap.
continuous.single-regression-coefficient: Entered coefficient/SE inputs are checked through metafor::rma.uni() in the standard random model.
continuous.generic-effect: Entered effect/SE inputs are checked through metafor::rma.uni() in the standard random model. The R object has no distinct provenance field for this and the entered-coefficient representation.
continuous.two-arm-means: Raw two-arm mean/SD/sample-size inputs are checked for MD and SMD through metafor::escalc() in standard models; SMD is also checked across cumulative, leave-one-out, subgroup, and bootstrap workflows.
continuous.two-arm-smd: The same raw two-arm means are checked for SMD through metafor::escalc().

diagnostic.diagnostic-counts: Raw TP/FN/FP/TN inputs are checked for Sens, Spec, PLR, NLR, and DOR standard models; all five metrics are covered by inverse-variance/random-effects fits, MH by DOR/PLR/NLR, and Peto by DOR. Cumulative, leave-one-out, and subgroup comparisons include DOR for all four methods and Sens/Spec/PLR/NLR for inverse-variance/random-effects, plus PLR/NLR for MH.
diagnostic.diagnostic-entered-effects: Entered DOR effect/SE inputs are checked through metafor::rma.uni(); the joint Reitsma model remains raw-count-only.

binary.standard: All four methods are compared for OR. Inverse-variance/random-effects also cover RD, RR, AS, YUQ, YUY, and all five one-arm measures PR/PLN/PLO/PAS/PFT; Mantel-Haenszel is compared for RR and RD. Random-effects also covers entered OR and one-arm PR effects.
binary.cumulative: All four methods / OR; every prefix is compared to a direct metafor fit and labels retain source order.
binary.leave-one-out: All four methods / OR; the full set and every omission are compared to direct metafor fits in source order, including one-study Peto omissions.
binary.subgroup: All four methods / OR; each subgroup and overall fit is compared to direct metafor with study identity and order checks. Binary Peto uses raw-count requests without preseeded effects, including two one-study subgroups; plot effects are populated from the Peto fits.
binary.meta-regression: meta.regression / OR with one continuous moderator and with a continuous plus categorical moderator is compared to direct metafor formula fits.
binary.bootstrap: All four methods / OR on raw two-arm counts use 32 identically seeded boot.ma resamples compared draw-by-draw to direct metafor fits. binary.random also checks 90% intervals against boot::boot.ci(); its boot.meta.reg subtype checks 32 coefficient draws, coefficient means, and 90% normal intervals with one continuous moderator.

continuous.standard: continuous.fixed and continuous.random are compared for raw MD and SMD. continuous.random also covers raw TXMean, entered coefficient, and generic entered-effect representations.
continuous.cumulative: continuous.fixed and continuous.random are compared for SMD and raw TXMean; every prefix is compared to a direct metafor fit and labels retain source order.
continuous.leave-one-out: continuous.fixed and continuous.random are compared for SMD and raw TXMean; the full set and every omission are compared to direct metafor fits in source order.
continuous.subgroup: continuous.fixed and continuous.random are compared for SMD and raw TXMean; each subgroup and overall fit is compared to direct metafor with study identity and order checks.
continuous.meta-regression: meta.regression / SMD with one continuous moderator and with a continuous plus categorical moderator is compared to direct metafor formula fits.
continuous.bootstrap: continuous.fixed and continuous.random use 32 identically seeded boot.ma resamples on raw two-arm SMD and raw one-arm TXMean inputs; every draw is compared to a direct metafor fit.

diagnostic.standard: diagnostic.fixed.inv.var and diagnostic.random cover Sens, Spec, PLR, NLR, and DOR; diagnostic.fixed.mh covers DOR, PLR, and NLR; diagnostic.fixed.peto covers DOR. Existing public mada tests cover diagnostic.reitsma for standard and meta-regression.
diagnostic.cumulative: All four univariate methods / DOR; every prefix is compared to a direct metafor fit and labels retain source order, including the one-study Peto prefix. Inverse-variance/random-effects also cover Sens, Spec, PLR, and NLR; MH covers PLR and NLR.
diagnostic.leave-one-out: All four univariate methods / DOR; the full set and every omission are compared to direct metafor fits in source order, including one-study Peto omissions. Inverse-variance/random-effects also cover Sens, Spec, PLR, and NLR; MH covers PLR and NLR.
diagnostic.subgroup: All four univariate methods / DOR; each subgroup and overall fit is compared to direct metafor with study identity and order checks, including singleton Peto subgroups. Inverse-variance/random-effects also cover Sens, Spec, PLR, and NLR; MH covers PLR and NLR.
diagnostic.meta-regression: diagnostic.reitsma is covered by the existing public mada authority tests.

independent_authority_evidence.remaining_authority_matrix_gaps: All 50 method/workflow cells have representative direct authority comparisons, but metric and input-representation intersections remain partial. Binary cumulative/leave-one-out/subgroup cases still use OR only; raw non-OR and one-arm measures are standard-only, entered non-OR effects are unverified, and MH coverage beyond OR is RR/RD only. Continuous entered coefficient/generic effects and raw MD are standard-only; TXMean sequential/bootstrap comparisons use raw one-arm means, while entered TXMean is unverified outside the standard random model. Diagnostic non-DOR sequential/subgroup comparisons use raw counts; entered effects are checked for DOR only in the standard random model. Meta-regression covers a continuous moderator and a continuous-plus-categorical model, but interactions and other moderator combinations are not covered. boot.ma covers the declared binary/continuous method workflows on raw count/mean representations; entered-representation boot.ma cases are unverified. boot.meta.reg is checked only for binary.random OR with one continuous moderator; the continuous subtype and categorical-bootstrap regression remain unverified. boot.meta.reg.cond.means is a legacy internal subtype with missing helpers, no app producer or method-parameter selector, and is now rejected at the public request boundary rather than treated as a supported capability. The separate v0.3.1 tagged-source reference contains 11 cases; the direct embedded-package API reference contains only the 14 casewise mappings in verification.release_package_api_v031. Neither fills remaining intersections or establishes packaged executable, GUI, or human/platform parity.
eligibility_and_api_notes: Peto cases use OR/DOR only; binary Mantel-Haenszel authority evidence beyond OR covers RR and RD, while diagnostic Mantel-Haenszel covers DOR/PLR/NLR.
One-arm binary measures use raw event/total counts with inverse-variance/random-effects methods; two-arm effect measures and model eligibility differ by estimator.
Reitsma consumes complete raw diagnostic counts; entered diagnostic effects are not eligible for the joint model.

The Python diagnostic subgroup worker puts cov_name in params; the R validator resolves both this GUI request shape and the documented string selected.cov override to a CovariateValues object. The matrix checks both forms, rejects an unknown covariate at validation, and compares each form's subgroup fits to direct metafor results.

boot.meta.reg.cond.means is not declared by the application workflow contract or selectable through method parameters; its legacy R branch has missing helper functions. Public bootstrap requests using this subtype are rejected by rcmetar.validate.analysis.request.

small_study_effects.evidence_kind: Direct source-level R-driver comparisons to public authority calls. The test uses pkgload::load_all and does not depend on rpy2.
small_study_effects.authority: Pinned meta 8.5-0 public metabin/metacont/metagen/metabias/trimfill calls; direct metafor::regtest for the mixed-effects Egger extension.

method_coverage.binary.OR: Harbord, Peters, and Rucker AS+RE fit statistics, coefficient/SE/CI, roles, and method-specific model names are compared to independent meta 8.5-0 calls. The displayed Peters infinite-precision estimate and interval are parsed and compared to the public intercept and confidence interval.
method_coverage.continuous.MD: Classical Egger and Begg-Mazumdar are compared to meta::metabias; mixed-effects Egger coefficient, intercept, and both intervals are compared to metafor::regtest. Common/random pooled display summaries and the selected display model are compared to a direct meta::metacont fit. Displayed classical and mixed Egger infinite-precision rows are compared to each authority's intercept and interval.
method_coverage.continuous.SMD: Pustejovsky-Rodgers coefficient, standard error, test, confidence interval, and study count are compared to meta::metacont plus meta::metabias(method.bias="Pustejovsky").
method_coverage.diagnostic.DOR: Deeks regression output is compared to meta::metabin plus meta::metabias(method.bias="Deeks"); the generated funnel artifact is checked for x=1/sqrt(ESS), y=log(DOR), direct ESS predictor/weights, and weighted fit line.
method_coverage.trim-and-fill: Random-effects L0 OR left/right scenarios and MD automatic-side scenario compare imputed count, study labels, augmented effects/SEs, display center, and displayed estimate/interval to direct meta::trimfill calls. Output is labeled as sensitivity analysis.

small_study_effects.eligibility_and_study_identity: The raw OR fixture contains 13 named rows; the final double-zero row is excluded and the exact included.indices are asserted as rows 1 through 12 before comparing against the matching direct authority model. A nine-study subset verifies that Harbord, Peters, and Rucker AS+RE stay unavailable with the explicit below-10 reason.
small_study_effects.limits: This is deterministic numerical authority evidence, not a frozen RCMetaR 0.3.1 output fixture or a saved/reopened desktop journey. Other eligible measures/designs, trim-and-fill estimator/model/side combinations, missing-data policies beyond the named double-zero OR row, plot geometry beyond the Deeks axes, and packaged export/reopen behavior remain unverified.
